[quote=corzerran;61556682]Cecilia sat with a quiet contentedness in the passenger seat. She was glad to be with her love once again. There was a tiny hint of nervousness in her voice as she spoke; she knew that things would go well, but meeting the parents of Elena still made her a little bit skittish.

[i]"So have you told them about [b]us[/b] yet? Or are we going to do that now?"[/i][/quote]
Elena looked at Cecilia, expression blank with thought, [i]"Oh.. well, I don't think I've told them that I was dating again, the last they knew I was forever a single woman."[/i] She chuckled  and opened her door.

She started grabbing food from the trunk with Zana. Nika lingered with Cecilia to offer a reassurance, [i]"Don't worry too much about the in-laws, they've got about as much bite as she does."[/i]

[b]MILITARY SKIRMISH IN SOUTHEAST - 6 DEAD[/b]

[pre][NAYPINAU - 15 MAY 2028] Earlier this evening, a sudden military skirmish arose between a Lyuongoan National Army patrol and a mercenary group owned by the Lyuongoan Mining Corporation (LMC) in the southeast, about 10 miles northeast of Ryuloga. What started the incident is unclear as of this moment, a LMC spokesperson claimed in an interview with a national television provider that the patrol trespassed on mining grounds, while General Hein Wei, overseer of Army movements in the southeast, claim that LMC-paid militias raided a LNA camp. The LMC has vehemetly denied this claim, and is currently pressuring the resignation of the long-tenured and venerated Hein Wei for quote "dangerous slandering of the company name." President Tung Aung released a statement earlier that him and his cabinent will look through the case and will do, quote, "what is necessary." The People's Congress is split on the issue, as both the army and mining corporations hold large sway in both chambers. No matter the conclusion, this is sure to be a lose-lose situation for the President, whose regime has long faced problems with balancing national loyalties and mining company handouts.[/pre]

[b]VETERAN GENERAL HEIN WEI FIRED BY PRESIDENT, MINING COMPANIES TO BLAME[/b]
[pre][NAYPINAU - 16 MAY 2028] Lyuongo President Tung Aung officially released a statement Tuesday morning officially releasing General Hein Wei from his duties. General Hein cut his teeth in the Lyuongoan Jungle, a hotspot for insurgents and organized crime syndicates alike. The now former General Hein was an adamant opposer to the Lyuongoan Mining Corporation's acquisition of independent mercenary groups in 2019, instead insisting on patrolling the southeast himself. The LMC's board of execs constantly feuded with Hein over the next decade, eventually boiling and crackling last night, ending in a skirmish between the two. As of tonight, 8 are confirmed dead, 12 wounded. Among the dead are 6 of Hein's own men. 

Pressure from interest committees and the military has effectively split the government, with President Tung now thrust in the unfortunate position of having to straddle an unruly military back together. However, one could make the case that this is a better predicament than if the Uranium mining corps turned against him. As Hein heads back to his hometown of Furinau, only time will tell what lies ahead for the Republic.[/pre]

[i][u][b]The Transition[/b]
[/u]
On May 17, 2028, the United States of Oceanica initiated changes within the government through internal reform. It was officially announced as a response to the increasing instability in the world and the economy about to face internal effects of what comes from increasing global conflict. The push of initial actions was focused on protecting vital industries, strengthening financial systems, and hastening national security cooperation. The actions were initially to ensure the transition of an illiberal technocratic democracy operating under tough times. Power began to be concentrated in the executive organization and councils that brought together the top members of the government with industry and high tech leaders. No announcement has been made to the public, but the public information is that reform has been passed. With the past,  the United States of Oceanica has remained strong economically, with rapid technology advancement, and has quickly reformed the government's institutions to adapt and react to an emergency crisis. It also maintained a relatively consistent level of trust with its people, even though others disagree, but this resulted in no significant issues. Democratic institutions were in place, but they were no longer as influential as the growing executive and technocratic groups. Decisions were now made in a bureaucratic meeting before they were announced.
[/i]

[quote=nederlandse_staat;61551510][Spoiler=first offensive]
[I]With most of the proper airfields heavily damaged/destroyed the rest of the jets are relocated towards the north of the country to protect the already heavily decentralized weapons industry from missile attacks. Crude airfields are build and the Trapdoor jets have their landing gears modified to land on highways and on dirt runways.
In the underground secret labs the question kept persisting:[/i] 
[B]how to disrupt hochdeutsche radio communications?[/b]
[I]Scientists quickly found the answer: look at information and photo's of the growler's jamming pod online and make a smaller land-based jammer that can be mounted on a light truck or trailer based on any information found.
Work and research quickly started on a truck-mounted jamming pod. 

Despite fuel and munition sources being buried undeground missiles kept hitting it. To finally put an end to it, the fuel and ammo is further dispersed and buried atleast 18 to 25 meters under the ground and accessed via elusive tunnel networks.To keep getting fuel the AAO set up operation ant's nest to smuggle fuel into the country. With a large part of the imports happening via the north to have the advantage of hiding the transports in the thick jungles and forests of south vespuria. 
With growlers and compass call jamming the radio's despite the attempts to counter it. A new solution is to install ultra-wide band into military radio's and radars, that way making them more resistant to jamming and making full-spectrum overwhelm impractical without massive power expenditure from the growlers/compass call. Alongside that the burst transmissions start to get randomized timings with a few getting embedded with noise like signal to evade the wideband monitoring. Some radio platoons start to swap radio signatures a lot, sometimes 2 to 4 times in a hour.
Anti-air regiments across the country start to mass-adapt decoy emitters to draw away missiles. The decoys designed to match army radars. Another order iss end out to the decentralized factories in the north or right across the border in no-man's land, install Infrared guidance in CIWS and other AA. Alongside that more CIWS is ordered to thin out harpy swarms before impact, specifically of the SVK marksman type that uses 25mm air-burst rounds. To reinforce the CIWS in taking down the drones the AAO and defence ministry unveil something that is in the works for a few years, the Tijmman Aldhûs, a High-power microwave (HPM) weapon developed to disable drone swarms and SEAD missiles by frying their electronics, the HPM is Named after Donald Aldhûs. The HPM is either mounted on the back of a standard Ruisgen 4X4 truck or mounted on top of a GGV9 chassis. Already 4 units of the GGV9 variant are build with atleast 30 more of the ruisgen 4X4 variant about to be ordered. 2 of the 4 units is already deployed, the aldhûs HPM having taken out a significant portion of several kamikaze drones and missiles, both subsonic and supersonic during test trials several months ago. Anyways, the AAO starts to carry out large cyber attacks to disrupt regional communications on land. 

With the HDF going to the capital the army starts to try and thin out the convoys as much as possible via hit-and-run attacks by either tank platoons, kamikaze drones, militia, or a mix of the three. the center is quickly abandoned in order to not let any historical buildings get damaged by the fight. But in the outskirts the first convoys get ambushed by a large amount of soldiers and militia's who fire RPG's at the engine or turret of several tanks after getting inside the minimum zone of their APS. Further more kamikaze drones start to get deployed in large swarms to overwhelm any defenses of the invading convoys with some of the kamikaze drones attacking in angles where APS has a hard time reaching. To deal with any attack helicopters the army uses LVS Flyswatter MANPADS, which is integrated with a very sensitive matrix imager and resistant to flares, to shoot them down. The attackers quickly disperse before air support can target them while sniper traps in the outskirts start to target hochdeutsche NCO's and officers.[/i]

[B]sint-jonathanwaard. 01:37[/b]
[I]Several partisan regiments are awaiting the signal for the first offensive since the war. The goal? Kill as much marineinfanterie and destroy as much equipment as possible. Retaking land is secondary. The clock hits 1:40 and the partisans start the attack on a nearby docked supply ship belonging to the HDF. They plunder the ship for supplies and leave afterwards. 

Across the occupied territory many partisan uprisings start to happen, supply lines start to get harassed and raided more frequently and with much more intensity, any marineinfanterie patrols that gets spotted gets ambushed. Alongside that the partisan regiments move around the territory frequently to keep harassing the marineinfanterie.
in the east 10000 royal marines get deployed for the first time since the invasion started. Using infiltration tactics to destroy small outposts and bases. To reinforce the attrition offensive the 1st and 2nd coastal defense regiment starts to use drones to patrol the coast for any supply ships belong to the Hochdeutsche with a truck mounted anti-ship battery waiting for coordinates and moving into a different spot when the missile is fired. 
To add pressure onto the marineinfanterie the army starts launching night time guerilla attacks and more kamikaze drones against the HDF around the capital, mainly targeting their armored vehicles and anti-air in groups or by sneaking up to an armored vehicle and slamming into it's engine to disable it. Artillery mounted on flatbed trucks with their chassis reinforced starts to slowly get used more to compensate the country's lack of dedicated SPG's. These 'SPG's' (mostly armed with 105mm or 122mm howitzers) support the offensive by shelling the convoys with guided shells or cluster munition and move away to a different spot after firing. On top of that several cruise missile launchers starts to fire a few dozen subsonic and supersonic missiles at multiple targets inside the occupied zone. Mostly command and control centers, ammo depots and any airfields used by the HDF to supply their forces via air. The missiles zero in on their targets and smash into them despite some missiles being shot down.
With the offensive now fully going, (light) attack helicopters start doing strafing attacks at night only, targeting artillery systems, outposts and any cluster of unfortunate marineinfanterie by flying below the treeline and only emerging for attacking positions.
26000 militia and reserves at the moment get send to the front to reinforce the assymetrical defenses. 
With the war going on the foreign ministry reaches out to Neudresden to ask which date the first round of peace talks can start and in which country it will happen.
When asked about Hochdeutsche presence around Zuidhoven the foreign minister only replied: 
"just because an enemy nation occupies the capital doesn't mean the war is over for now."[/i][/spoiler]
